newsitem.title: UK: UK Panel to probe way BZW gave info on bid.
newsitem.headline: UK Panel to probe way BZW gave info on bid.

text.p: The UK's Takeover Panel, which polices mergers and acquisitions activity, said on Monday it would probe the circumstances in which information was received from investment bank BZW during the hostile bid by CE Electric for Britain's Northern Electric.

"The executive will investigate the circumstances in which information was received from BZW, possibly having a bearing on certain purchases of Northern shares, subsequent to consultation with the executive and a hearing before the full panel on December 18," it said in a statement.
BZW is advising Northern in its defence.
The panel said that following the investigation its executive would "consider what, if any, further action is appropriate".
BZW's role has been under scrutiny since it emerged that it had not initially disclosed a 250,000 stg payment from Northern in addition to its 1.5 million stg fixed fee.
A BZW spokesman told Reuters the firm had not done anything wrong in accepting what he said was a "discretionary fee".
He denied there was any link between the fee and BZW's purchase earlier in the week of Northern shares to bolster its client's defence against the U.S. predator, CE Electric.

The panel now has to decide whether to accept BZW and Northern's appeal against an extension of the offer period which it granted last Friday and which resulted in CE Electric achieving the required level of shareholder support to win its bid.

The offer period was extended to 1300 GMT on Tuesday. On Monday morning CE Electric said it had acceptances for 50.13 percent of Northern shares, compared with 49.77 percent by the original close date on Friday.
